backyard bird habitat birds/backyard-habitat.md # backyard bird habitat

a bird-friendly yard offers food, water, shelter, and places to raise young. native plants are especially useful because they support local insects and produce seeds, berries, and cover.

## habitat elements

- **native plants:** provide food and structure throughout the year.
- **water:** a clean, shallow bird bath can attract visitors.
- **shelter:** dense shrubs and evergreen cover provide refuge.
- **food:** if using feeders, clean them regularly and place them where birds have nearby cover but are protected from window collisions.

## visitors to look for

you may see [[birds/northern-cardinal]], [[birds/blue-jay]], and [[birds/black-capped-chickadee]].

## observation question

which habitat feature seems to attract the greatest variety of birds in your area?

birds/bald-eagle.md

bald eagle birds/bald-eagle.md # bald eagle

the bald eagle is a large bird of prey associated with lakes, rivers, and coastal areas. it is the national bird of the united states.

## identification

adults have a dark brown body, white head and tail, and a large yellow bill. immature birds are mostly brown and take several years to develop adult plumage.

## feeding and habitat

bald eagles primarily eat fish when available, but they also take waterbirds and carrion. they often nest in large trees near water.

## connections

eagles are one example of a raptor. their habitat needs connect to [[birds/backyard-habitat]], although their territories are much larger than a typical backyard.

bird migration birds/bird-migration.md # bird migration

bird migration is the regular seasonal movement of birds between breeding and non-breeding areas. the timing and distance vary by species.

## why birds migrate

migration can help birds reach areas with seasonal food supplies and suitable breeding conditions. day length, weather, food availability, and inherited behavior can all influence timing.

## what to observe

- changes in which species appear in your area.
- large movements during favorable weather.
- birds feeding heavily before departure.
- differences between spring and fall migration.

## related notes

start with [[birds/birdwatching]] to record sightings. local food and shelter are discussed in [[birds/backyard-habitat]].

birds/birdwatching.md

birdwatching birds/birdwatching.md # birdwatching

birdwatching is the practice of observing wild birds and learning to recognize them by appearance, behavior, calls, and habitat.

## a simple observation routine

1. pause and listen before moving.
2. look for movement in trees, shrubs, water, and open ground.
3. note the bird's size, shape, colors, and behavior.
4. record the location, date, weather, and habitat.
5. compare observations with [[birds/northern-cardinal]] and [[birds/black-capped-chickadee]].

## useful equipment

- binoculars
- a small field notebook
- a bird identification guide
- a camera or phone for reference photographs

## related ideas

bird activity changes with the seasons. see [[birds/bird-migration]] and [[birds/backyard-habitat]].

birds/black-capped-chickadee.md

black-capped chickadee birds/black-capped-chickadee.md # black-capped chickadee

a small, active songbird common across much of the northern united states and canada.

## identification

- black cap and bib.
- white cheeks.
- gray wings and back.
- buff-colored sides.

## behavior

chickadees move actively through branches, often hanging upside down while searching for insects and seeds. they may visit feeders and take one seed at a time.

their familiar call sounds like *chick-a-dee-dee-dee*. the number of dee notes can vary with context.

## connections

chickadees are useful birds to watch during winter. see [[birds/birdwatching]] for observation tips and [[birds/backyard-habitat]] for ways to support them.

birds/blue-jay.md

blue jay birds/blue-jay.md # blue jay

the blue jay is a conspicuous songbird known for its blue, white, and black plumage, crest, and loud calls.

## identification

- blue upperparts with black barring on the wings and tail.
- white underside and a black necklace across the throat.
- a noticeable crest that can rise or flatten.

## behavior

blue jays eat nuts, seeds, insects, and other food. they can carry and cache acorns, helping move oak seeds away from parent trees.

their calls are varied and often carry over long distances. they may imitate the calls of other birds.

## connections

blue jays and [[birds/northern-cardinal]] may both visit backyard feeders. their food choices connect to [[birds/backyard-habitat]].

birds/northern-cardinal.md

northern cardinal birds/northern-cardinal.md # northern cardinal

the northern cardinal is a familiar songbird in the eastern and central united states. it is often seen in gardens, woodland edges, and neighborhoods.

## identification

- **shape:** stout body, long tail, and prominent crest.
- **male:** bright red overall with a dark face around the bill.
- **female:** warm tan or brown with reddish accents in the wings, crest, and tail.
- **bill:** thick, cone-shaped, and orange-red.

## behavior

cardinals commonly visit feeders for seeds. they often forage in pairs or small family groups and may sing from exposed branches.

## connections

compare its feeder behavior with the [[birds/blue-jay]]. for a habitat perspective, see [[birds/backyard-habitat]].

getting started notes/getting-started.md # getting started

this is your personal knowledge garden. capture thoughts, questions, observations, plans, and things you learn. each markdown file becomes a note in the graph.

## connect thoughts

write `[[birds/birdwatching]]` or `[[birds/northern-cardinal]]` to link notes. linked notes become connected dots in the graph. a note can have several tags, but its first tag determines its primary graph cluster.

> [!note] static publishing
> github pages hosts the files but cannot write edits back into the repository. edit markdown locally or in github, then commit and push.

## add a note

create a `.md` file anywhere under `content/`. add yaml frontmatter:

```yaml
---
title: my note title
tags:
  - ideas
  - personal
---
```

then run `npm run build-index` and commit the updated `content/index.json`.
